tasks.short: Read the sold design, schedule crews and customers, check the design against codes, notify the grid operator, coordinate the day and check the handover file.

steps.what: Installation manager reads the signed quote and roof design
Installation manager plans installation dates with crews and customers by phone and spreadsheet
Installation manager checks string sizes, roof distances and protection against codes by hand
Installation manager registers the system with the grid operator
Installation manager coordinates installations on the day with the crew lead and customer
Installation manager checks the test results and handover file for conformance

tasks.design: A planning board in the installer's {ERP} proposes crew and date by rules on skills, region and crew availability, and sends the customer a date to confirm; the manager adjusts. Fixed code rules run on the design (string voltage within inverter limits, roof edge distances, protection devices) and list only the failures; grid registration, coordination on the day and the handover check stay with the manager.
tasks.previous_blocker: Planning lived in a spreadsheet and phone calls; code checks were done from memory and tables.
tasks.enabler_now: Construction ERP apps plan staff and subcontractors, and design tools hold the full layout as data.
tasks.still_hard: Weather and roof surprises upset plans; rules cover only the checks that can be written down.
tasks.human_edge: Juggling crews when rain cancels two days and every customer wants their date.
tasks.altitude: The manager adjusts proposals and handles failures; responsibility for code conformance stays with the manager.

evidence.claim: A construction ERP plans staff, subcontractors and equipment from the budget.
Building installations, PV systems included, must meet the national electrical installation standard.
Rule-based crew planning on skills and region is not high-risk AI; a model ranking workers on behaviour would be.

assumptions: Boundary: from the signed quote to the accepted handover; sales and design are outside.

Input contract: crew skills and regions kept by the installation planner; code rules written and kept by the company's technical lead; design data exported from the design tool; fallback is spreadsheet and hand checks.
Customer time is outside the manager's savings.
Grid registration, coordination and handover checks do not change.
unknowns: Whether the design tool exports full string data.
research_questions: Which code failures does the rule check catch that hand checks missed?

already_counted.description: Installation manager reviews listed code failures.

incremental.description: Installation manager reports rules that give false failures.
Technical lead keeps code rules current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Firms with few crews or unusual roofs keep planning and checking by hand.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Visit sites, brief crews on roof safety, check subcontractor certificates, inspect with a checklist and correct unsafe work.

steps.what: Installation manager visits sites and supervises solar installers at height and on electrical work
Installation manager briefs crews on fall protection before roof jobs
Installation manager collects subcontractors' certificates and safety plans by e-mail
Installation manager fills in a paper site inspection checklist
Installation manager stops and corrects unsafe work to ensure compliance with safety standards

tasks.design: Subcontractors upload certificates and safety plans to a {PARTNER_PORTAL} that tracks expiry dates and blocks planning when one is missing; the manager reviews what is flagged. Site inspections use a phone checklist with photos in the contractor's site app ({OTHER}), recorded per crew; supervising, briefing and correcting stay on site.
tasks.previous_blocker: Certificates arrived by e-mail and inspections were paper forms.
tasks.enabler_now: Construction apps keep checklists, site diaries and defect reports on phones.
tasks.still_hard: Safety depends on being on the roof and seeing it; forms do not make work safe.
tasks.human_edge: Stopping a job when the anchor point looks wrong, even if the crew is behind.

reach.learn: Whether expiry tracking stops jobs starting with lapsed certificates.

evidence.claim: Construction software keeps site diaries, checklists, handovers and defect reports.
For works with special hazards, a health and safety plan of hazards, measures and agreements is filled in as work progresses.
Records of output per worker observe performance and need works council consent; inspections here are per crew.

assumptions: Boundary: from site visits to unsafe work corrected; incident investigation is outside.
Input contract: subcontractors upload their own documents; checklist items set by the company's safety advisor; fallback is e-mail and paper.
Subcontractor time is outside the manager's savings.
Supervising, briefing and correcting do not change.
research_questions: Do photo checklists show recurring safety gaps across crews?

already_counted.description: Installation manager reviews flagged subcontractor documents.

incremental.description: Installation manager learns the checklist app.
Safety advisor keeps checklist items current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Most of this task is being on site, which does not change.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Read the roof layout and survey, count materials, estimate crew and days, choose access equipment and order shortfalls.

steps.what: Installation manager studies the site survey photos and roof layout
Installation manager counts panels, rails, hooks, cables and inverters in a spreadsheet to estimate materials
Installation manager estimates personnel and days from experience
Installation manager chooses scaffold, lift or roof hooks for access
Installation manager checks stock and e-mails the wholesaler an order for shortfalls

tasks.design: The solar design tool ({OTHER}) builds the materials list from the roof layout and the central product catalogue, and labour norms per panel count, roof type and storeys give a first crew and day estimate for the manager to adjust. Shortfalls against stock in the {ERP} become a draft purchase order to the wholesaler; reading the survey and choosing access equipment stay with the manager.
tasks.previous_blocker: Materials were counted from drawings and labour estimated from memory.
tasks.enabler_now: Solar design tools hold the layout and a product catalogue, and turn layouts into quotes with variants.
tasks.still_hard: Roof surprises (rot, asbestos, weak rafters) change the job; labour norms need upkeep.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing from the survey photos that this roof will take an extra day.
tasks.altitude: The manager checks and adjusts estimates instead of counting.

reach.learn: Whether the same norms make quotes more accurate.

evidence.claim: A solar design tool designs PV systems with yield estimates and keeps a central product catalogue with price rules.
A solar tool turns a 3D roof layout into a branded quote with variants.
A construction ERP plans staff and equipment from the budget.

assumptions: Boundary: from the roof layout to materials ordered; the sales quote is outside.
Input contract: product catalogue kept by purchasing; labour norms kept by the operations manager from past jobs; stock levels kept by the warehouse in the ERP; fallback is counting by hand.
Wholesaler time is outside the manager's savings.
Survey reading and access choices do not change.
unknowns: Whether the design tool exports materials lists.
How accurate past labour estimates were.
research_questions: Do norm-based estimates beat experience on days per job?

already_counted.description: Installation manager checks generated materials lists.
Installation manager adjusts norm-based crew estimates.

incremental.description: Installation manager reports where norms were wrong after jobs.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Firms doing many unusual or commercial roofs keep estimating by hand.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Take installers' technical calls, look up manuals and diagrams, visit for hard problems, explain fixes and share lessons.

steps.what: Installation manager takes installers' calls about solar electric, thermal and mechanical systems
Installation manager searches manuals, datasheets and wiring diagrams for the answer
Installation manager drives to the site for problems that cannot be solved by phone
Installation manager explains the fix and checks it from photos the installer sends
Installation manager shares lessons from solved problems with the other crews

tasks.design: Manufacturers' manuals, datasheets, wiring diagrams and the company's known-issue notes go into one searchable library in {DOCS}, filtered by the products on each job, which installers can open on their phones. Simple look-ups no longer need a call and the manager finds pages faster; site visits, explaining fixes and checking them stay with the manager.
tasks.previous_blocker: Manuals were PDFs scattered over e-mails and websites, so installers phoned the manager.
tasks.enabler_now: Searchable document libraries on phones are standard; job product lists come from the design.
tasks.still_hard: Electrical faults need expertise; a manual page is not a diagnosis.
tasks.human_edge: Hearing from an installer's description what is really wrong with the string.

reach.task: Solve common faults on the roof
reach.learn: Whether installers solve more themselves with job-filtered manuals.

evidence.claim: Searchable document libraries filtered by product cut look-up time for field technicians.
Work on the installation must meet the national electrical installation standard.

assumptions: Boundary: from an installer's question to the fix checked; warranty claims are outside.
Input contract: manuals and datasheets collected by purchasing from manufacturers; known-issue notes written by the manager; job product lists from the design tool; fallback is phoning the manager.
Installer time is outside the manager's savings.
Site visits, explaining and sharing lessons do not change.
unknowns: Share of calls that are simple look-ups.
research_questions: How many calls do installers stop making once they have the library?

incremental.description: Installation manager writes known-issue notes for the library.
Purchasing adds manuals for new products.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Firms with experienced crews get few look-up calls.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The installation manager keeps site safety, problem solving and coordination; counting, scheduling and look-ups move to rules and libraries.
skills_to_grow: Keeping code rules and labour norms current
role.ambitious_version: A manager who is on the roofs where it matters while the schedule, materials and manuals take care of themselves.
